title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. k is a subfield of C and M is a category of motives over k of finite type, possibly mixed (the inserted word 'mixtes' is uncertain). M is implicitly a Tannakian category. It has two fibre functors:
(1) T_DR : M -> finite-dimensional k-vector spaces. This is algebraic de Rham realisation, carrying the Hodge filtration (and the weight filtration in the mixed case).
(2) T_B : M -> Q-Hodge structures -> finite-dimensional Q-vector spaces. This is the Betti realisation and depends on the embedding k into C.
(3) The comparison isomorphism phi : T_B (x)_Q C ≅ T_DR (x)_k C. Grothendieck first wrote 'compatible with filtrations' and then struck it out, rightly, since T_B (x) C carries no filtration of its own.

The period torsor.
- G = Aut_(x)(T_B) is the motivic Galois group over Q, in its Betti incarnation.
- (4) P = Isom_(x)(T_B (x)_Q k, T_DR) is a right torsor under G_k.
- (5) T_DR is recovered as the twist P ×^{G_k} (T_B (x) k).
- The comparison (3) is exactly a C-point phi of P.
- Marginal remark: knowing (G, P, phi) reconstructs M = Rep_Q(G) together with (1), (2) and (3).
This is the period torsor formalism. The period conjecture (phi is a generic point of P, so trdeg of the periods equals dim G) is not stated on this page, but this is precisely the setup for it.

Recovering the Hodge data. The triple (G, P, phi) loses the filtration, so Grothendieck adds group-theoretic data:
- (6) T_Hdg = gr T_DR, a bigraded fibre functor over k. The bigrading is (p,q) with p from F and p+q the weight.
- (7) G'_k = P ×^{G_k} G_k = ad(P) ≅ Aut_(x)(T_DR), the inner form of G_k given by de Rham.
- (8) H' is the subgroup of G'_k preserving the filtration and acting trivially on the graded pieces.

Next page.
- H' is unipotent.
- Q = Isom_(x)(T_DR, T_Hdg) inducing the identity on gr is an H'-torsor, i.e. the torsor of splittings. It is trivial over a field of characteristic 0.
- G'' = Aut_(x)(T_Hdg).
- The bigrading gives two cocharacters i_1, i_2 : G_m -> G'' with eps∘i_j = id and i_1·i_2 = i (the weight cocharacter). These are the k-rational avatars of the Deligne torus cocharacters z, z̄.
- Grothendieck then lists data a)–g): G with weight and Tate maps; G''; i_1, i_2; the unipotent torsor; P; the identification of ad(P) with G'; and phi in P(C).
The aim is a purely group-theoretic description of a motivic category with its Betti, de Rham and Hodge realisations and comparison.
errors: The first gloss 'compatible avec filtrations' for (3) is meaningless as T_B⊗C has no filtration; Grothendieck struck it himself.

Identifying 'the Hodge structure on T_B' with 'the bigrading of T_B⊗C' is right only for pure motives. For mixed motives a mixed Hodge structure is not a bigrading. It needs W and F, and Deligne's splitting is not canonical over Q. So if 'mixtes' is intended, gr must be taken for both W and F, and H' should fix both.
The Hodge decomposition of T_B⊗C is recovered from the filtration on T_DR⊗C only by also using complex conjugation on T_B⊗C (H^{p,q} = F^p ∩ conj F^q). This is implicit, not written.
The remark that (G,P,phi) reconstructs M assumes M is neutral Tannakian with fibre functor T_B (equivalence M ≅ Rep(G)). This was not established in 1965 and is conjectural for genuine motives.

ideas.what: Category of motives over k with Betti and de Rham fibre functors and a comparison isomorphism; motivic Galois group G = Aut⊗(T_B)
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group / Tannakian category of motives with realisations
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra, Demazure, Kleiman; Récoltes et Semailles discusses motivic Galois group

ideas.what: P = Isom⊗(T_B⊗k, T_DR) as a G_k-torsor with T_DR as twist and the comparison isomorphism as a C-point phi ∈ P(C)
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor (torseur des périodes); underlying Grothendieck's period conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, 1960s, reported by André); formalised by Deligne, André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004), Kontsevich–Zagier 2001, Nori
ideas.where_published: Only a footnote attribution (Lang's 1966 transcendence book, André's book); not in Grothendieck's own texts to my knowledge

ideas.what: Reconstruction of the motivic category with both realisations and comparison from (G,P,phi)
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of a category with two fibre functors via a bitorsor

ideas.what: Inner form G'_k = ad(P) = Aut⊗(T_DR), unipotent subgroup H' of filtration-preserving automorphisms trivial on gr, and torsor of splittings Q
ideas.modern_name: Unipotent radical of the parabolic attached to a filtered fibre functor; splittings of filtrations (Saavedra, Deligne's filtered fibre functors)

ideas.what: Hodge bigrading of gr T_DR encoded as two cocharacters i_1, i_2 of Aut⊗(T_Hdg) with product the weight cocharacter (continued on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Hodge cocharacter / Deligne torus S = Res_{C/R} G_m description of Hodge structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971, Hodge II 1971); Saavedra

missed.claim: An explicit 1965 written formulation of the de Rham–Betti period torsor P = Isom⊗(T_B⊗k, T_DR) under the motivic Galois group, with the comparison isomorphism as a C-point and the statement that (G,P,phi) recovers the category with its realisations. The literature credits the period conjecture to Grothendieck only by oral or second-hand attribution; this page documents the torsor formalism itself, years before Saavedra, Deligne, André and Kontsevich–Zagier.
missed.quote: P = Isom⊗(T_B ⊗_Q k, T_DR) sous G_k ... l'isom (3) définit une section canonique φ ∈ P(C) | La connaissance de G, P, φ permet de reconstituer M avec (1) (2) et (3)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical documentation of the origin of the period torsor and period conjecture framework (André, Huber–Müller-Stach, Brown's motivic periods).

missed.claim: The program, continued on the next page as data a)–g), of encoding the whole Betti/de Rham/Hodge package of a motivic category over k ⊂ C. The intended data are: G, an inner form over k, k-rational Hodge cocharacters i_1, i_2 on Aut(gr T_DR), a unipotent splitting torsor, and the period point. It is an abstract 'motivic Hodge datum' over the field of definition k rather than over C or R. It was never completed into a theorem.
missed.quote: Pour reconstituer la structure filtrée sur T_DR, et donc la structure de Hodge sur T_B ... il convient d'introduire (6) T_Hdg = gr* T_DR
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relates to descriptions of motivic Galois groups with Hodge-theoretic constraints. Examples are Mumford–Tate groups via k-rational cocharacters on de Rham and the filtered-torsor formalism used in p-adic Hodge theory and period theory. It is mostly subsumed by Saavedra and Deligne's later work.

deep.surprise_reason: The period torsor and the reconstruction from (G,P,phi) appear explicitly and early (1965). Their attribution to Grothendieck is known but poorly documented, which makes this valuable historical evidence. The Hodge-data part anticipates Saavedra and Deligne's cocharacter formalism but is incomplete. None of it is mathematically new today.
transcription_corrections: Line (2): the struck word is 'Modf(Q)' replaced by 'Str. Hodge', and the functor is written T_B (overwritten from 'T_Bdg' or similar) — transcription essentially right.
The struck phrase under (3) reads 'compatible avec filtrations, sur 2 membres' (crossed out).
Item (6) reads 'T_Hdg : M → Mod Bigrad f(k)', i.e. finite bigraded k-modules, with ':' rather than '∈'.
(8): 'est groupe des Aut de T_DR respectant la filtration et qui induisent l'identité sur le gradué associé' — correct.
